subject: Operational warranty & maintenance boundary negotiation - Order Form X
summary: Procurement at Triton Cloud pushed back on warranty/maintenance language. Internal team proposes uptime metric clarifications, a stepped service-credit schedule, 48-hour maintenance notice, and a narrow operational warranty scope. Technical definitions (regional vs global measurement) and carveouts are requested. External accepted most items pending a single warranty sentence redline and DocuSign exchange.
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@tritoncloud.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@tritoncloud.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operational warranty + maintenance boundary — Order Form X

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Procurement reviewed the draft Order Form and has two sticking points we'd like to resolve before legal will sign:

1) Operational warranty: The draft includes a broad warranty that references "continuous availability" and an open-ended remedy clause. Our counsel wants the warranty narrowed (e.g., limited to availability remedies and exclusion of consequential damages tied to third-party infra). Can your legal team suggest wording that limits warranty to the service availability SLA and a 30-day remedy window?

2) Maintenance boundary & notice: We need clarity that scheduled maintenance windows will not exceed X hours/week and that maintenance excluded from uptime will only apply if we receive at least 48 hours' calendar notice. Also want assurance around blackout windows for our business-critical hours (M–F 08:00–12:00 PT).

We've attached a short procurement note (Procurement_Request.pdf) with redline highlights.

If we can get alignment on warranty scope and the maintenance notice/blackout approach, procurement is prepared to route to legal for signature. Can we get proposed language by Tuesday? If helpful, we can hop on a 30-min call.

Best,
Elena Martinez
Director, Strategic Procurement
Triton Cloud

Attachment: Procurement_Request.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@tritoncloud.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational warranty + maintenance boundary — Order Form X

Elena —

Thanks for the clear note and the procurement attachment. We've reviewed internally and pushed back where appropriate; attached is an annotated redline set and a short proposal for warranty language. High-level responses below — full redlines in SLA_Redlines.docx and OrderForm_Annotated.pdf.

- Warranty: We can narrow the warranty so it references only the "Service Availability" metric as defined in Section 2 and limits remedies to the service credit schedule (30-day cure/remedy window). We will add explicit language disclaiming consequential damages arising from third-party infrastructure failures. Proposed sentence included in SLA_Redlines.docx.

- Maintenance & notice: We can accept that scheduled maintenance is excluded from uptime only if Redwood provides >=48 hours' calendar notice and specifics on affected regions/services. We will commit to limiting planned maintenance to no more than 16 hours per calendar month per region (we're proposing this cap — happy to discuss).

- Blackout windows: We can mark your M–F 08:00–12:00 PT window as a customer-designated blackout and guarantee we will avoid scheduled maintenance during those times for production resources (subject to emergency exceptions with immediate notification).

- Service credits: Proposed stepped matrix in SLA_Redlines.docx (99.99%: 0.5x monthly invoice; 99.9%: 0.25x; below 99.5%: 1x) — we kept the banding conservative to balance operational risk.

Next steps: I asked Kimberly to review the warranty/legal phrasing; Rachel will validate the billing/credit math. If these redlines look workable, we'll route a short legal-approved paragraph for your counsel and prepare DocuSign routing.

Would you be available Wed 28th 09:00–09:30 PT for a quick alignment call?

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Ops — Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA_Redlines.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document), OrderForm_Annotated.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational warranty + maintenance boundary — technical clarifications

Quick technical clarifications to make the legal redline precise (copying here so procurement/legal have clean language we can paste into the Order Form):

- Uptime measurement: We measure "Service Availability" per region (region-level rolling 30-day window) unless the customer purchases cross-region failover. So the SLA should say "per region unless otherwise specified"; avoids disputes if one region has localized maintenance.

- Scheduled maintenance carveout: Define "scheduled maintenance" as maintenance that is communicated >=48 hours in advance and listed in the regional maintenance calendar. Emergency maintenance (security hotfixes, P0 mitigations) should be excluded but with immediate notice and post-mortem.

- Response times: Propose tying P1/P2 response commitments to the customer's support tier in the Order Form (P1 = 1 hour for enterprise, 2 hours for standard; P2 = 4 hours / 8 hours).

- Rolling upgrades: Rolling upgrade windows where individual racks or pools are cycled should be a separate carveout and not count as a full-region outage provided per-instance request-level latency stays within the published thresholds.

I'll attach a short CSV with metric definitions for legal to reference.

—Aditya
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Attachment: metric-defs.csv (text/csv)
From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@tritoncloud.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@tritoncloud.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Oct 2026 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational warranty + maintenance boundary — Order Form X

Grace / team —

Thanks for the quick turn. Procurement reviewed your redlines and the technical clarifications from Aditya. We are largely aligned: the 48-hour notice, the per-region SLA phrasing, and the blackout window carveout are acceptable. The service-credit bands look reasonable.

Only outstanding item: our legal team requested a small tweak to the warranty sentence to explicitly limit Redwood's warranty to remedies under the SLA and to add a cap equal to the cumulative service credits for the affected billing period (i.e., warranty remedy capped at the applicable service credit amount). If you can accept that cap language, procurement will hand the package to legal and we can sign.

Please send the final 1–2 paragraph warranty/legal snippet and the Order Form DocuSign link and we'll route it internally. Proposed DocuSign routing: Elena Martinez (Director), Procurement Ops (procurement@tritoncloud.com).

Elena
Director, Strategic Procurement
Triton Cloud

Related: DocuSign link (placeholder): https://docusign.com/XYZ-OrderFormX
